_note: The code step of the Arduino Foundations levels (issue #58), by level position. It comes after the wiring tasks. task: the line in the task list. goal: what lib/sketch/goal.ts tests: "blink" (the LED is on for on_ms, then off for off_ms, again and again) or "button" (the LED is on only while the button is pressed). led: a part id on the board, or uno.L for the small LED marked L on the Uno (it is on pin 13). led_name: the name of the LED in the reason of a fail. starter: the first code, one string for each line. solution: the full sketch that "Write it for me" puts in the editor (issue #145), one string for each line. steps: Step by step (issue #144), the lines of the sketch in order: line (the code, with its indent), goal (what the line does, in simple words, with no code of the line), accept (more answers that pass), hint (a tip in words). Write the text in ASD-STE100.

2.task: Write the sketch: make the LED blink once each second.
2.goal_text: Make the LED on pin 13 blink: on for 500 ms, then off for 500 ms, again and again. That is one blink each second.
starter: // Blink: the LED on pin 13 turns on and off, once each second.
// Make pin 13 an output, so it can give power to the LED.
digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH); // The LED turns on.
// To do: turn the LED off, then wait again.
solution: // Blink: the LED on pin 13 turns on and off, once each second.
digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH); // The LED turns on.
digitalWrite(ledPin, LOW);  // The LED turns off.
hints: digitalWrite(ledPin, LOW); turns the LED off.
One blink each second: 500 ms on and 500 ms off. 500 + 500 = 1000 ms.
loop() runs again and again. After the last line, it starts again at the top.

steps.goal: Give pin 13 a name, for example ledPin. Use const int, because the pin does not change.
steps.hint: A const int line has 4 parts: const int, the name, = and the value. Put a ; at the end.

steps.goal: Start setup(). It runs one time, when the Uno starts.
steps.hint: A function line has void, the name of the function, ( ) and a {.

steps.goal: Make the LED pin an output, so it can give power to the LED.
steps.hint: Use pinMode. It needs two values in ( ): the pin and the mode, with a comma between them.

steps.goal: Close setup().
steps.hint: Each { needs a } to close it.

steps.goal: Start loop(). It runs again and again, after setup().
steps.hint: It is almost the same as the first line of setup(). Only the name is different.

steps.goal: Turn the LED on.
steps.hint: Use digitalWrite. It needs the pin and HIGH or LOW. HIGH gives power to the pin.

steps.goal: Wait 500 ms (half a second).
steps.hint: Use delay. It needs the time in milliseconds.

steps.goal: Turn the LED off.
steps.hint: This line is almost the same as the line that turns the LED on. LOW stops the power.

steps.goal: Wait 500 ms again. Then loop() starts again at the top.
steps.hint: 500 + 500 = 1000 ms. That is one blink each second.

steps.goal: Close loop(). The sketch is complete.
steps.hint: Each { needs a } to close it.

3.task: Write the sketch: turn on the L light of the Uno while you press the button.
3.goal_text: The Uno has a small LED marked L. It is on pin 13. Make it turn on while you press the button, and turn off when you let go.
starter: // Button: the L light on the Uno turns on while you press the button.
const int ledPin = 13; // The small LED marked L on the Uno.
// To do: make buttonPin an input, with the pull-up resistor inside the Uno.
// A pressed button joins pin 2 to ground, so the pin reads LOW.
// To do: turn the light on.
delay(10); // A short pause, so the Uno does not run with no pause.
solution: // Button: the L light on the Uno turns on while you press the button.
const int ledPin = 13; // The small LED marked L on the Uno.
pinMode(buttonPin, INPUT_PULLUP); // The pin reads HIGH when nobody presses the button.
// A pressed button joins pin 2 to ground, so the pin reads LOW.
delay(10); // A short pause, so the Uno does not run with no pause.
hints: pinMode(buttonPin, INPUT_PULLUP); turns on the pull-up resistor inside the Uno. Then the pin reads HIGH when nobody presses the button.
digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH); turns the light on.
While the sketch runs, press the button on the board to test it.

steps.goal: Give pin 2 a name, for example buttonPin. The button is on pin 2.
steps.hint: A const int line has 4 parts: const int, the name, = and the value. Put a ; at the end.

steps.goal: Give pin 13 a name, for example ledPin. The L light of the Uno is on pin 13.

steps.goal: Make the light pin an output.
steps.hint: Use pinMode. It needs the pin and the mode.

steps.goal: Make the button pin an input, with the pull-up resistor inside the Uno.
steps.hint: Use pinMode again. The mode with the pull-up resistor is INPUT_PULLUP.

steps.goal: Close setup().
steps.hint: Each { needs a } to close it.

steps.goal: Start loop(). It runs again and again, after setup().
steps.hint: It is almost the same as the first line of setup(). Only the name is different.

steps.goal: Read the button pin, and keep the value in a new variable, for example state.
steps.hint: Make an int variable. Its value comes from digitalRead, with the pin in ( ).

steps.goal: If the value is LOW, do the next line. A pressed button joins pin 2 to ground, so it reads LOW.
steps.hint: Use if, with the test in ( ) and a { after it. To compare two values, use ==.

steps.goal: Turn the light on.
steps.hint: Use digitalWrite with the light pin. HIGH gives power to the pin.

steps.goal: Close the if. Then start else: the part that runs when the button is not pressed.
steps.hint: Put the } of the if, the word else, and a new {, all on this line.

steps.goal: Turn the light off.
steps.hint: LOW stops the power.

steps.goal: Close else.
steps.hint: Each { needs a } to close it.

steps.goal: Wait 10 ms, so the Uno does not run with no pause.
steps.hint: Use delay. It needs the time in milliseconds.

steps.goal: Close loop(). The sketch is complete.
